## Development

From `/workspace`: `python3 check.py submission` prepares the supplied wheels
offline and replays the public fixtures through bounded children.  The graded
suite is larger; the public fixtures are sanity checks only.  The public runner
spawns its child with `start_new_session`, so a sandbox that also denies
`setsid` to the (unsandboxed) developer shell reports `infrastructure_error`
before any candidate runs; that is an environment limit, not a candidate
failure.  Everything else here — aggregate budgets, exact comparison bands,
the full 218432-operation request and the 1GiB/32-FD/120s rlimits — was
exercised with the same child flags and limits directly.
